text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Over 2,000 council workers in the mining town of Ndola went on strike on Monday to push for a 100 percent pay rise and new conditions of service.
- Zambia's population is growing at an annual rate of between 3.2 and 3.5 percent, and could jump to 24 million from eight million by the year 2025 if measures are not taken to control it.
- The Zambia Confederation of Chambers of Commerce and Industry and the Confederation of the Indian Industry on Monday signed a cooperation agreement to boost trade between their two countries.
- Up to 33 percent of Zambians in urban areas are believed to be infected with the HIV virus, the Danish project, MS-Zambia, said in a report released on Monday.
